title: Demo · Theft under the BNS, no charge sheet after 60 days
story: Accused-1 is charged under BNS 303(2) for a shop theft on 09.08.2026, so the new codes (BNS and BNSS) apply. He was first remanded on 12.08.2026 and the police have not filed a charge sheet, so the 60-day period for default bail has run out; he has one other theft case pending and no co-accused.

steps.title: Rights Radar
steps.caption: At intake Peshkar ran the 7 rules of the Rights Radar on the dossier as of 2026-11-15: date arithmetic and statute tables, not the language model. Default bail: ELIGIBLE, Undertrial limit (BNSS s.479): NOT_YET, Production within 24 hours: CHECK and Antil category: A. Each result names its rule and the dates it used; rules not yet re-checked against the bare act are marked unverified.

filled.label: Default bail
filled.value: ELIGIBLE: 60-day limit (maximum 5 years). Day 1 is the first remand, 12.08.2026. It is day 96 and no charge sheet is on record. The right arose on day 61 (11.10.2026); an application must be made before a charge sheet is filed.

filled.label: Undertrial limit (BNSS s.479)
filled.value: NOT_YET: 96 days in custody. The threshold is 609 days for a first-time offender (1/3 of 5 years, on bond) and 913 days otherwise (1/2, on bail). The applicable threshold (1/2) of 913 days is reached on 09.02.2029, 817 day(s) from now.

filled.label: Production within 24 hours
filled.value: CHECK: Produced the next day; times not on record.

filled.label: Antil category
filled.value: A: Maximum punishment is 5 years: category A (up to 7 years). Antil's categories decide how an accused who was not arrested during investigation and cooperated is treated after the charge sheet; for a client in custody this is context, not a bail entitlement.
